abstract: Earlier papers in this sequence established a structural dictionary in which Dirac delta distributions arise as singular limits of finite projection kernels, admissibility filters, survivor-basin effects, and bookkeeping kernels. The execution bridge paper then identified the canonical finite kernel selected by Modal Triplet Theory (MTT) fixed-point data: the proper-time coherent kernel generated by the same operator that governs stabilization. The present paper applies that kernel to the first contact-loop calculation. We study the Euclidean scalar one-loop tadpole I_0^{(d)}(m)=\int_{\mathbb R^d}\frac{d^d k}{(2\pi)^d}\frac{1}{k^2+m^2}, which is ultraviolet divergent for d\ge 2, and replace the point-contact propagator by the MTT proper-time filtered propagator \Delta_\tau(k)=\frac{e^{-\tau k^2}}{k^2+m^2},\qquad \tau>0. We prove that I_\tau^{(d)}(m)=\int_{\mathbb R^d}\frac{d^d k}{(2\pi)^d}\frac{e^{-\tau k^2}}{k^2+m^2} is finite for every d, m>0, and \tau>0, and derive the exact Schwinger representation I_\tau^{(d)}(m) =(4\pi)^{-d/2}\int_0^\infty e^{-m^2 s}(s+\tau)^{-d/2}\,ds. In four dimensions this gives the closed form I_\tau^{(4)}(m) =\frac{1}{16\pi^2}\left[ \frac{1}{\tau} -m^2 e^{m^2\tau}E_1(m^2\tau) \right], with the local-limit asymptotics I_\tau^{(4)}(m) = \frac{1}{16\pi^2} \left[ \frac{1}{\tau} + m^2\bigl(\gamma+\log(m^2\tau)\bigr) +O(m^4\tau|\log(m^2\tau)|) \right]. Thus the MTT coherence scale \tau gives a definite finite correction and an effective ultraviolet scale \Lambda_{\rm eff}\sim \tau^{-1/2}. The divergent local theory is recovered as the singular limit \tau\downarrow0. Renormalization is therefore not abolished; rather, the usual local counterterms are reinterpreted as the subtractions needed when the finite coherent kernel is forced into the zero-width contact limit.
title: MTT-Corrected Contact Loops and Finite One-Loop Tadpoles Proper-Time Coherent Kernels, UV Softening, and the Local-Limit Counterterm
